scenes.say: Ever wonder when to use normalization versus dimensional modeling? Let's break down the difference so you can ace your next interview.

scenes.label: Normalize
scenes.sub: Organizes data to reduce redundancy and boost integrity.
scenes.say: Normalization is for online transaction processing. It cuts down redundancy and keeps your data clean.

scenes.label: Dimensional
scenes.sub: Structures data for fast analytics using facts and dimensions.
scenes.say: Dimensional modeling is built for analytics. It shapes data into facts and dimensions for fast reporting.
Picture this: normalized means separate tables for customers and orders, linked by foreign keys. Dimensional means a central sales fact table, surrounded by dimension tables.

scenes.question: Is normalization better for analytics?
scenes.wrong: Yes, less redundancy is always best.
scenes.right: No. Dimensional modeling is better for analytics because it speeds up queries and reporting.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: is normalization better for analytics? Not really. Dimensional modeling is what you want for fast queries.
